packageRules.description: Webtor components: keep the tag, bump the digest, one PR each. Automerged once the smoke checks pass — by the time a digest lands here the same build has already been serving production webtor.io, so green CI is the only remaining question. Renovate merges these itself on a later run (platformAutomerge off) rather than relying on GitHub native auto-merge, which would require branch protection.

Base images (alpine, nats, nats-box, versitygw, plus nginx in the test compose): non-major bumps are grouped into one PR, wait 7 days after the upstream release so regressions surface elsewhere first, then automerge on green smoke. Unlike webtor components these never ran anywhere before landing here, hence the bake time.

Base-image majors (e.g. an alpine version bump changes musl/openssl for every binary in the image): a human reads the release notes first. The PR is only created after it is approved on the dependency dashboard, and is never automerged.
